title: Warm-up: floor division from C division
starter:
%a = param 0 dtype=i32
%b = param 1 dtype=i32
# div truncates toward zero. Build Python-style floor division from div, mod, cmplt, xor, where, add (no sub: add %q -1).
%out = div %a %b
hints: Truncating division and floor division only disagree when the result is negative and the division isn't exact.
Compute `q = div a b` and `r = mod a b`. Floor needs `q - 1` exactly when `r` is nonzero and `r` and `b` have opposite signs.
Build those two conditions as bools: nonzero is `r < 0` xor `0 < r`, and opposite signs is `r < 0` xor `b < 0`. Pick with `where`, using `where cond second-bool false` as an AND.

answer.code:
%a = param 0 dtype=i32
%b = param 1 dtype=i32
%q = div %a %b
%r = mod %a %b
%rneg = cmplt %r 0
%rpos = cmplt 0 %r
%nz = xor %rneg %rpos
%bneg = cmplt %b 0
%signs = xor %rneg %bneg
%fix = where %nz %signs false
%q1 = add %q -1
%out = where %fix %q1 %q
answer.explain: C-style `div` rounds toward zero, which is one too high exactly when there is a remainder whose sign differs from the divisor's. The reference detects that with `cmplt` and `xor`, combines the two conditions with a `where` that acts as AND, and subtracts one only then. `INT_MIN div -1` wraps the same way in both forms.
